paper_identity.title: Adverse Effect of the Duration of Antibiotic Use Prior to Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors on the Overall Survival of Patients with Recurrent Gynecologic Malignancies

planning_summary: This paper provides real-world clinical evidence supporting the hypothesis that antibiotic-induced gut dysbiosis negatively impacts ICI efficacy, specifically manifesting as reduced Overall Survival rather than immediate lack of disease control. It offers specific data on the threshold of antibiotic duration (>14 days) associated with adverse outcomes in gynecologic cancers, serving as a concrete example of the 'antibiotic-microbiome-ICI' interaction axis.
scope_interpretation_cautions: The association between antibiotics and OS is observational; confounding by indication (severity of infection requiring longer antibiotics) cannot be fully excluded.
The study does not measure gut microbiota directly; conclusions about dysbiosis are mechanistic hypotheses based on external literature.
Results are specific to anti-PD-1 monotherapy in gynecologic cancers and may not generalize to combination therapies or other solid tumor types without verification.
